en: Now listen to part two of the interview.
zh: 现在请听访谈的第二部分。

en: Questions 6 to 10 are based on part 2 of the interview.
zh: 第6至10题根据访谈的第二部分提问。

en: In My Poets, you write about attending readings, and socializing with writers, and the energy or tension of those face-to-face encounters.
zh: 在《我的诗人》中，您写到了参加朗诵会、与作家交往，以及这些面对面接触带来的活力或紧张感。

en: But in interviews, you've also said that you think that it’s “a tremendous gift to be lonely in poetry”.
zh: 但您在访谈中也说过，对诗歌创作而言，“孤独是一份极大的馈赠”。

en: Could you talk about that?
zh: 您能谈谈这一点吗？

en: I really think this comes down to one’s temperament.
zh: 我觉得，这归根结底取决于一个人的性情。

en: Other writers are much more readily sociable creatures.
zh: 其他作家往往更乐于社交。

en: They feel there’s a kind of continuity between their writing life and their social life.
zh: 他们觉得，写作生活与社交生活之间存在某种连续性。

en: I never experienced things that way at all.
zh: 我完全没有过那样的体验。

en: Could you tell us why?
zh: 您能告诉我们为什么吗？

en: For me, poetry was not a zone about professionalization or networking.
zh: 对我来说，诗歌并不是一个以职业化或建立人脉为中心的领域。

en: There are many, many different kinds of writerly engagement, but I feel that people should be given permission not to engage.
zh: 作家与外界互动的方式有很多很多种，但我觉得，人们也应该被允许不参与其中。

en: There’s so much pressure to find a community, and one wants a community — but community may not come from the people organizing the poetry reading.
zh: 寻找一个群体的压力很大，人们也确实渴望有一个群体；但这个群体未必来自那些组织诗歌朗诵会的人。

en: It might be found among the folk musicians playing down there in the street.
zh: 你也可能在街头演奏的民间音乐人那里找到这个群体。

en: A community for poets is not necessarily other living poets.
zh: 诗人的群体不一定就是其他在世的诗人。

en: Another question.
zh: 换个问题。

en: How do you arrange the poetry in your books?
zh: 您是怎样安排诗集中各首诗的顺序的？

en: I notice that they’re all divided into sections, and all end with a concluding part.
zh: 我注意到，它们都分成若干部分，而且最后都有一个结尾部分。

en: My last two books, for instance, This Blue, have central sections that speak to a complex set of associations with particular places.
zh: 比如，我最近的两本书，包括《这片蓝》，都有位于中间的部分，涉及与特定地点相关的一组复杂联想。

en: It’s also the case that some of the poems are so strongly voiced that if I were to begin with them.
zh: 有些诗的声音或表达方式又特别鲜明，以至于如果我拿它们作为开篇……

en: People might think the entire book is in that one mode, and I wanted to avoid that.
zh: 人们可能就会以为整本书都是那一种风格，而我想避免这种情况。

en: And I often write sequences.
zh: 我还经常写组诗。

en: So I almost think of the sections more musically.
zh: 所以，我几乎是在从音乐的角度思考这些部分的。

en: Emm, Emm...
zh: 嗯，嗯……

en: And I’m interested in ushering people through a series of mental and tonal landscapes, of sound- and thought-worlds.
zh: 我希望引导读者走过一系列精神与声调的景观，走过声音和思想的世界。

en: For good or ill, my books have not tended to be that narrative.
zh: 不论这是好是坏，我的书一直都不太偏重叙事。

en: Is this the reason that each section has a concluding part?
zh: 这就是每个部分都设置结尾的原因吗？

en: I think a concluding stanza marks a kind of “sending forth of the book” to the world.
zh: 我认为，结尾的一节诗标志着一种把这本书“送入世界”的方式。

en: It also allows you to back away from something, to modulate out of certain kinds of intensities, and to gesture maybe to something in the future.
zh: 它还让你能够从某些东西中退后一步，从某种强烈的情绪中缓缓转出，并且也许向未来的某种事物作出示意。

en: It can either restate a note, or it can refer to something more broadly.
zh: 它可以重申一个基调，也可以指向更广阔的内容。

en: Do you have a particular approach to reading your own poetry aloud?
zh: 您朗读自己的诗时，有没有某种特定的方法？

en: Well, you can get locked into your own sense of things, and your way may not be the best way to read that poem.
zh: 你可能会被自己固有的理解束缚，而你的方式未必就是朗读那首诗的最佳方式。

en: You can get a little muscular contraction on your face.
zh: 你的面部可能会出现一点肌肉收缩。

en: One doesn’t want to have facial tics, one doesn’t want things to be routinized, and I think about that.
zh: 人们不希望自己出现面部抽动，也不希望一切都变成固定套路，我会思考这些问题。

en: Sometimes people are surprised by my reading.
zh: 有时候，人们会对我的朗读方式感到惊讶。

en: I remember a poet said to me, “Oh, your poems are a lot funnier than I thought they were.” He was being very nice, but I didn’t know how to take that!
zh: 我记得一位诗人对我说：“哦，你的诗比我想象的好笑多了。”他的态度很友善，但我当时不知道该怎么理解这句话！

en: Ha ha ha...
zh: 哈哈哈……

en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

en: Maureen, thank you so much for being with us today.
zh: 莫琳，非常感谢您今天参加我们的节目。

en: Pleasure.
zh: 很荣幸。

en: This is the end of part two of the interview.
zh: 访谈的第二部分到此结束。

zh: 第6至10题根据你刚才听到的内容提问。
